bib.title: Retentive Network: A Successor to Transformer for Large Language Models

question: Can one architecture combine training parallelism, O(1) inference cost and Transformer-level language-modeling quality?
hypothesis: A retention mechanism with parallel, recurrent and chunkwise forms breaks the 'impossible triangle' and succeeds the Transformer.
contributions: Retention: dual recurrent/parallel form derived from recurrence, with a chunkwise recurrent form
Multi-scale retention with per-head fixed decay, swish gate and GroupNorm
Experiments at 1.3B-6.7B on scaling, zero/4-shot, training cost, inference cost, 200M variants comparison, ablations

method.summary: Replaces multi-head attention with gated multi-scale retention (decayed linear attention with xPos-style rotation, no softmax). Trained from scratch at 1.3B, 2.7B, 6.7B against same-size Transformers with matched parameters, on 100B tokens; also 200M comparison with Linear Transformer, RWKV, H3, Hyena.

datasets.name: Curated mix of The Pile, C4 and The Stack
datasets.preprocessing: <bos> token appended at start of each sequence

datasets.name: HellaSwag, BoolQ, COPA, PIQA, Winograd, Winogrande, StoryCloze

other.gamma: 1 - exp(linspace(log 1/32, log 1/512, h)), same across sizes

models.name: 200M comparison models (Linear Transformer, RWKV, H3, Hyena, RetNet)

training.lr_schedule: linear decay in text; Table 7 says polynomial decay
training.hardware: 512 AMD MI200 GPUs (pretraining); 8x Nvidia A100-80GB for cost tests

inference.samples: single run per configuration; no seeds stated
inference.prompting: zero-shot and 4-shot; prompt format not given

other.cost test: 6.7B on one A100-80GB, lengths 2048-8192, batch 1-8 for latency; Transformer uses KV cache

metrics.name: Validation perplexity
metrics.definition: perplexity on in-domain val set and OOD corpora
